description: Literature, supersonic aviation, animation, games, measurement, early aircraft, Scottish geography, wine country and ancient history drive a broad run of questions that rewards precise recall rather than comfortable familiarity.

s03e01.description: White chocolate provides the episode’s sweetest piece of trivia, though the question ladder itself is less forgiving. Food, culture and assorted general knowledge turn familiar things into precise distinctions, which is basically Millionaire’s preferred form of mischief.

s03e02.description: Dumas’s great tale of imprisonment and revenge supplies an appropriately dramatic title. Literature joins a broad question set where recognition comes easily, exact recall less so, and every confident memory seems to arrive carrying a small legal disclaimer.

s03e03.description: Concorde brings supersonic elegance to the question ladder. Aviation history gives the episode its sleekest subject while the quiz ranges elsewhere with rather less aerodynamic efficiency, forcing contestants to navigate facts at considerably below Mach 2.

s03e04.description: Mufasa gives the episode a regal dose of animated familiarity. Popular culture sits comfortably beside more traditional quiz material, proving that Millionaire has no ideological objection to making childhood memories compete directly with serious general knowledge.

s03e05.description: Solitaire becomes the episode’s neatly self-contained puzzle within a much larger puzzle. Games and everyday knowledge share space with broader trivia, and something normally associated with passing time suddenly acquires the gravity of a studio decision.

s03e06.description: ‘Nearest whole inch’ turns mundane measurement into an unexpectedly memorable phrase. The episode thrives on exactly that kind of precision: questions that seem harmless until a unit, definition or tiny wording choice becomes the entire problem.

s03e07.description: The Sopwith Camel flies in from early aviation history, instantly giving the episode a wonderfully specific identity. Machines, history and general knowledge mix on a ladder where knowing that something existed is merely the opening bid.

s03e08.description: Blaise Pascal brings mathematics, philosophy and scientific history into a single name. The episode’s wider question set remains cheerfully eclectic, but Pascal supplies the kind of learned reference that makes Millionaire briefly resemble an exam nobody revised for.

s03e09.description: The Isle of Skye provides a scenic pause in an otherwise unforgiving knowledge ladder. Scottish geography becomes the episode’s anchor while the questions roam elsewhere, because apparently even imaginary travel must be interrupted by multiple-choice uncertainty.

s03e10.description: Chile’s Colchagua Valley gives the episode a distinctly vinicultural detour. Geography and specialist knowledge meet in one elegant place-name, surrounded by the usual unpredictable shuffle of subjects that makes preparation for Millionaire essentially impossible.

s03e11.description: Alexander the Great marches into the question set with considerably more confidence than most people bring to the hot seat. Ancient history supplies the episode’s headline figure while the rest of the ladder ranges across less conquerable territory.
